findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet, which exposes the MySQL service to untrusted networks and greatly enlarges attack surface for a data store.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and snapshots, leaving stored data unprotected at rest.

The master username is hard-coded as 'admin' and the password is passed via a Terraform variable that is written in cleartext into state and interpolated into EC2 user data; the default privileged account name plus a plaintext-handled password weakens database access control.
No parameter enforcing TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport) is set and the application connects with mysqli_connect without SSL, so database traffic including credentials can travel in cleartext.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database endpoint, username and the plaintext DB password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host and is stored unencrypted in the API.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with the web application on this host and its overly permissive instance profile, an SSRF could retrieve role credentials and the secret-bearing user data.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption is configured, so the instance volume holding the credential file dbinfo.inc may be stored unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached to an internet-facing web server's instance profile, compromise of the host yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 and RDS resources in the account.
The RDS security group, via its egress rule, allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted outbound channel usable for data exfiltration or command-and-control.
Egress rule permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, removing outbound network segmentation controls.
